newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb blast damages Corsican bank, no injured.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast damages Corsican bank, no injured.

text.p: A bomb exploded at a bank in northern Corsica overnight, causing significant damage but no injuries in the second such attack in two nights, gendarmerie para-military police said on Sunday.
It said the device shattered windows and damaged the entrance of the Credit Agricole branch in the town of Calenzana.
A bomb placed on an outside cash dispenser of the Banque Populaire Provencale et Corse in the town of Ile Rousse wrecked the bank's computers and furniture on Friday night.

A few minutes later, gendarmes found a charge of dynamite placed on a cash dispenser outside a Credit Agricole branch in the nearby seaside resort of Balagne, whose mayor is Veterans Affairs Minister Pierre Pasquini. It was defused.
No one claimed responsibility for the three acts, which resembled previous actions carried out as part of a long-running campaign by separatist guerrillas seeking greater autonomy from France.
